question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) if a sum of ₹400 is borrowed for 5.5 years at 16% per annum rate of interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Rate % = Rate × Time

Effective Rate % = 16% × 5.5 = 88%

Simple Interest = Effective Rate % of Principal

⇒ SI = 88% of 400 = (88 ÷ 100) × 400 = 352

**∴ The correct answer is ₹352.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹400

Rate of Interest (R) = 16% per annum

Time (T) = 5.5 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 
 

 
 
 Simple Interest Calculation
 
 
 P = ₹400
 
 
• 
 T = 5.5 yrs
 R = 16% p.a.
 
 
 SI = ?
 
 
 SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = (400 × 16 × 5.5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 4 × 16 × 5.5

⇒ SI = 64 × 5.5

⇒ SI = 352

**∴ The correct answer is ₹352.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) after a certain time is the sum of the Principal (P) and the Simple Interest (SI).
Formula: A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100]

Compound Interest (CI)

Unlike Simple Interest, Compound Interest is calculated on the initial principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods.
Formula: A = P × [1 + (R ÷ 100)]T, and CI = A − P

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for the same principal and rate is given by:
Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)²
